To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the degree of polarization of a wave scattered from an inhomogeneous medium is a function of the scattering angle and the polarization state of the incident wave; (2) the Mueller matrix of a wave scattered at an angle theta from an inhomogeneou medium can be obtained from the Mueller matrix measured at an angle phi by rotating the scattering medium by an angle (pi-theta)/2 and rotating the polarization state of incident wave by an angle phi.

(1) the Mueller matrix and the degree of polarization of inhomogeneous media can be measured in situ using the coherent-on-receive mode; and (2) the Mueller matrix is a function of the scattering angle only.
the Mueller matrix and the degree of polarization can be used to characterize the scattering properties of inhomogeneous media.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the scattering of electromagnetic radiation by rough surfaces and inhomogeneous media.
the measurement of the scattering properties of inhomogeneous media.
the development of millimeter-wave radar systems and the measurement of the scattering phase function of natural and manmade targets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two modes of the radar are identical.
the totally coherent and coherent-on-receive mode provide identical results.
the two modes of operation are identical and interchangeable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coherent polarimetric system is an effective tool for characterizing the Mueller matrix of objects of interest.
the coherent-on-receive mode is more suitable for field measurements than the totally coherent mode.
the 35 and 95 GHz radar systems are now capable of making accurate measurements of the Mueller matrix and the degree of polarization for any type of inhomogeneous media.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now use our millimeter-wave radar system for both laboratory and field experiments.
the coherent-on-receive mode can be used for in situ measurements of scattering and polarimetric characteristics of inhomogeneous media, such as vegetation, snow and soil.

we have demonstrated that the Mueller and scattering matrices of an inhomogeneous medium can be determined from measurements of the degree of polarization of the scattered wave as a function of angle of incidence, polarization, and frequency.
